summaries: The first {culture} families lit their hearths at {place}, and {founder} taught them to listen to the things they loved.
{founder} led the first {culture} families to {place}, and the world began to hear them.
Roads joined the hearths, and makers raced each other to build wonders that carried across valleys.
Lamps were lit along every road, and {founder}'s heirs made things the world still remembers.
A circle at {place} tried to command the world instead of asking it, and a war followed until the old roads closed.
Neighbors quarreled over who the world should answer, and the quarrel ended in quiet fields at {place}.

summaries: The world listened less for a while; people gathered in safe valleys and kept small crafts, songs and festivals alive.
Roads grew over and relics slept, but the {culture} kept their recipes and their songs.
Hearths are being relit, roads reopened, and wayfarers are setting out to see what the world remembers.
{founder}'s old hearth was relit at {place}, and wayfarers set out from it to rediscover the world.

founderSummaries: {founder} of the {culture} lit the first hearth at {place} and taught {craft} to anyone who would sit still long enough.
{founder} walked the first {culture} families to {place}, carrying a {form} that never let them lose the way.
{founder} founded {place} and was famous there for {value} long before anyone called it a {culture} virtue.
artifactSummaries: A {culture} {form} made at {place} in {era}, so well loved that the world began to answer it.
The {form} {maker} carried in {era}. It has been used every day since, and it hums about it.
A {form} from {place}, made in {era} and passed hand to hand ever since.
